pages.title: Introduction
pages.body:
At the station, a broken PC may be worth more than scrap. A damaged case can hide usable parts; a machine with missing parts may sell well after repair and reassembly.

Open damaged cases in the workroom, inspect the parts, and decide what to repair, replace or recycle. Assemble a compatible motherboard and case, run the power-on check, then find a buyer.

pages.title: Introduction (Continued)
pages.body:
WORKROOM: DISMANTLE, REPAIR, BUILD AND RECYCLE
Page 3: slot selection, E + left-click transfers, repair returns and partial auto-fill.
Pages 4-7: damaged cases, repairable items, material/cash repairs and batch recycling.
Pages 8-11: power-on checks, build profiles, examples and high-end premiums.

SERVER ROOM: PRODUCTION, CASH AND RISK
Page 12: quick start.
Pages 13-16: algorithms, pools, capacity and maintenance.
Pages 17-18: servers and the coin exchange.
Pages 19-20: auto-selling and the ledger.

Check tonight's plan and estimated returns before deciding how many machines to run.

pages.title: Quick Actions
pages.body:
Hold E and left-click to send shop inventory or container contents to the workroom. Workroom items return to their original position first, then try carried inventory. Full inventory cancels the move. Disabled throughout scavenging; restored in the shop. Does not trigger while dragging or typing.

Click an empty slot to select stock; click an occupied slot to inspect, double-click to return it. Search and combine Workroom/Storage/Shop sources. Category/tier menus select directly; type/state cycle. Esc closes the small menu first.

Double-click workroom items to fill only a matching empty slot in the top panel; recycling only adds to the list. Cases and boards have separate work areas; the central mat handles parts. Pale-yellow outlines indicate a fit.

Auto-fill places available compatible items even when some are missing. Minimum Necessary for boards includes one SSD; 0GB means no capacity floor. Custom can select zero SSDs. Installed items stay; assemble manually. Results appear at the top.

Repairs return to the original source by default; if full, the repaired item stays in its slot. Return can be disabled. Catalog Stock counts intact standalone items of the same model/tier across three sources, excluding installed parts.

pages.title: Opening a Case
pages.body:
A damaged case is a locked loot crate containing intact or broken parts.

Transfer it through storage to the workroom, put it in the case panel's body slot and click Disassemble. Internal items return together. Insufficient inventory space leaves the case sealed.

Contents and identities are fixed at generation; disassembly never rerolls them. Once opened, the empty damaged case is worth zero. Repair an empty T1-T3 case with materials. Opening and disassembly both use the workroom; no screwdriver is required.

pages.title: What Can Be Repaired?
pages.body:
T1-T3 bare motherboards and empty cases can receive body repairs. Disassemble the six part families first: bodies and some modules are repairable; chips and capacity modules must be replaced.

CPUs, GPU cores, SSD controllers and capacity chips cannot be repaired. Common bodies, fan rotors, thermal modules and cooler fan assemblies use cash repair.

Recycle broken CPUs of any tier, or emptied, unlocked T4/T5 broken boards and cases. Disassembled subparts are eligible intact or broken; disassemble whole parts first. Choose one of five materials; output follows the value budget.

A T2 motherboard body needs Electronic Parts and Wire. Repairs consume the entire recipe at once in the workroom, with no progress carried between attempts. The repaired body stays in its slot; broken internal parts remain broken.

pages.title: Repair & Recycling
pages.body:
BODY RECIPES: empty T1-T3 bodies only.
Board: T1 Electronic Parts; T2 adds Wire; T3 adds Nuts.
Case: T1 Scrap Metal; T2 adds Metal Ingot; T3 adds Printing Plastic. One of each listed material. The whole recipe must be available; no carried progress.

CASH REPAIR: the six common bodies, fan rotors, thermal modules and cooler fan assemblies cost 25% of saved intact value, rounded down; a nonzero value costs at least 1C.

CAPACITOR REPAIR: each broken 100/200W bank uses one Electronic Part and one Wire; 400/600W uses two of each; 1000W uses three. Workroom materials first, then storage. Intact banks consume nothing.

A PSU has a common body and 1-6 mixed capacitor banks. Total rated wattage of at least 100/200/400/600/1000W gives T1/T2/T3/T4/T5; above 1000W stays T5. Broken banks still count toward rated wattage; intact wattage is separate.

First disassembly: T1 has 100W x1, T2 100W x2; T3/T4/T5 have 200W x2/x3/x5. Existing builds return their actual banks.

pages.title: Repair & Recycling (Continued)
pages.body:
Cores, controllers and capacity chips cannot be repaired. GPU/RAM/SSD parts hold up to 6/6/4 capacity modules, with at least one required; capacities add from the actual installed modules.

Batch recycling accepts workroom or storage items, single-item drags or selected groups. Mix specifications and states, and adjust each quantity. The budget is 50% of total current value, or 125% with Efficient Use.

Choose one material; output rounds down by its unit price. Remainders are neither paid in cash nor carried forward. All output goes to the workroom. Less than one output or insufficient space leaves the entire batch untouched.

An irreparable broken item worth zero, or unable to produce one unit by itself, may be discarded without output.

pages.title: Power-on Check
pages.body:
Install CPU, CPU cooler, GPU, RAM and SSD on the board; install that board, a PSU and case fans in the case. Partial assemblies can be saved, but a complete PC must pass inspection before sale.

All installed parts must be intact. Multiple RAM modules must have the same configuration tier. The highest and lowest internal part tiers may differ by no more than three.

T1-T5 boards have 1/1/1/2/2 SSD slots and accept every SSD tier. A complete PC needs at least one storage device. T4/T5 boards support two GPUs; extra installed parts are also checked.

pages.title: Three PC Build Profiles
pages.body:
COMPLETE PC: +20%
Passes inspection without either special profile below.

VALUE BUILD: +30%
Every part except CPU, GPU and PSU must be below both CPU and GPU tiers. The PSU may be at most one tier below the higher of CPU and GPU.

BOTTLENECK BUILD: +10%
Both CPU and GPU are at least one tier below the highest tier of the other internal parts.

A PC receives only one profile.

The lower-district builder refuses Bottleneck Builds. Vesper accepts them when the case and all internal parts are intact T1-T3. The upper-district buyer refuses T1/T2 parts.

pages.title: Build Examples
pages.body:
VALUE BUILD
T3 CPU and GPU; T2 PSU and every other part. The higher-tier core parts qualify for the Value Build premium.

BOTTLENECK BUILD
T2 CPU and GPU; T3 PSU and every other part. Both CPU and GPU fall below the highest tier of the remaining internal parts.

Only one under-tier core part does not trigger Bottleneck Build. Compatibility and intact-state checks still apply.

pages.title: High-End Parts
pages.body:
Intact T4 CPUs/GPUs and T5 parts receive a 20% high-end premium. Performance parts determine the configuration tier; capacity chips and common parts do not lower it. Boards and cases use actual internal parts.

An intact case containing qualifying high-end parts inherits this premium once. Several qualifying parts do not stack it; removing the last removes it. Empty cases and damaged loot crates do not inherit it.

High-end and build-profile premiums can both apply, but their percentages cannot simply be added. The buyer's quote and bargaining still affect the final price.

pages.title: Server Room Quick Start
pages.body:
1. BUILD, CHOOSE A COIN AND POOL
Enter from the workroom, put a rig in an unlocked rack slot and install intact GPUs. Choose a coin and pool in room management. Start in Standard mode; check VRAM requirements and tonight's executable plan.

2. KEEP POWER MONEY, THEN SLEEP
Check tonight's plan and retain cash before sleeping. Review credited output and costs next day. Tomorrow's sales cannot pay tonight's power. Reduce running machines when capacity or cash is short.

3. SELL FOR CASH; STOP FOR SERVICING
Preview a coin sale before confirming. Keep money for future power and servicing. Stop low-maintenance rigs before servicing. Try auto-selling, overclock or server leases once familiar with the cycle.

pages.title: Rigs and Algorithms
pages.body:
CHECK ACTUAL PARTS FIRST
Open Rig Management, Operating Details and Algorithm Details to inspect each GPU's core tier, actual VRAM and exclusion reason. Rigs include support equipment and take only GPUs. Mixed GPUs are allowed; VRAM is never shared between cards.

THREE ALGORITHMS
Anchor and Singularity use Core: at least 4GB per GPU; extra VRAM adds no speed.
Matrix and Pulse use Memory Bandwidth: at least 8GB, full capability at 16GB.
Stellar uses Large VRAM: at least 16GB, full capability at 32GB.

Broken or undersized GPUs contribute no work and incur no GPU power cost. No eligible GPU means the rig stops.

pages.title: Network Competition and Pools
pages.body:
COMPARE NET OUTPUT AND COMPETITION
Output depends on effective hash rate and current difficulty. Network competition gradually changes difficulty. Compare output, coin price and power cost together: a high price does not guarantee higher profit. Displayed output already deducts mode rejection losses and pool fees.

POOL CHANGES APPLY NEXT DAY
Steady Pool deducts 2% of output. Variable Pool deducts 0.5%, with a 0.70-1.30 luck factor shared by the same coin on the same day. Coins arrive automatically after the next day's settlement; unsettled output cannot be sold.

Balances and tiny output remainders survive coin changes.

pages.title: Capacity and Operating Modes
pages.body:
CHECK TONIGHT'S PLAN AND STOP REASONS
Power includes device wattage plus 15% shared cooling overhead; cooling counts device heat only. Upgrade power and cooling separately. Both upgrades are needed to unlock the corresponding slots and case tiers.

Active leases reserve capacity first. Rigs are scheduled by priority, then slot number. Machines that cannot fit or cannot be paid for are skipped.

ECO / STANDARD / OVERCLOCK
Hash-rate multipliers: 0.82 / 1 / 1.12.
GPU-power multipliers: 0.70 / 1 / 1.35.
Base rejection: 0.2% / 0.5% / 2%.

Only enabled Auto-Downshift tries a lower mode for capacity shortages; it never shifts up. Use tonight's actual planned mode.

pages.title: Power Prices and Servicing
pages.body:
USE CASH ALREADY AVAILABLE
Base power costs 40C per kW per operating day, plus 15% cooling. The combined rig bill rounds up. After expansion 1, a +/-15% price event may be announced for tomorrow, lasting 3-5 days.

The shop's nightly costs are paid first; remaining cash schedules rigs. Tomorrow's coin sales cannot fund tonight. Stopped rigs pay no rig power and suffer no wear.

STOP, THEN SERVICE
Eco/Standard/Overclock wear is 0.6/1/2 per operating day. Below 60 warns; below 30 disables overclock and adds 3 percentage points of rejection. Zero triggers protective shutdown.

T1-T5 servicing uses 1/1/2/2/3 Electronic Parts and 5/8/12/18/25C. All costs are taken at once to restore maintenance to 100. Materials come from workroom and storage; shortages cancel it. Moving a rig or changing GPUs does not reset maintenance. Servicing does not repair broken parts.

pages.title: Servers and Prepaid Rent
pages.body:
CASH UPFRONT, SERVICE OVER TIME
Servers use CPUs and RAM; actual parts determine capacity. Choose 3/5/7-day leases with 0%/3%/5% bonuses. Signing locks configuration, reserves capacity and prepays the full term's power at the signing-day rate. Net cash rounds down for the whole lease. Power is not charged again during the term. Equipment cannot be removed or changed before expiry.

CASH RECEIVED IS NOT ALL EARNED
Prepaid cash can fund operations, but rent for future service remains unearned. The ledger recognizes rent by service day and lists prepaid power and whole-order rounding separately. A seven-day advance is not first-day net profit.

pages.title: Coin Market and Trade Depth
pages.body:
PREVIEW BEFORE CONFIRMING
Reference quotes are valuation guides. Execution depends on today's depth and cumulative net buys/sells; splitting orders does not remove slippage. Each side pays 1%. Whole cash totals round up for buying, down for selling. A sale netting less than 1C is rejected; keep accumulating.

NORMAL INPUT: 0.0001 COIN
Wallets retain units of 0.000001 coin. Normal inputs use 0.0001-coin steps; Sell All handles wallet remainders. A manual order beyond depth must be resized and confirmed again; it never silently executes part of the order.

After settlement, quote or asset changes, use a fresh preview. Reference market value is not immediately cashable net proceeds.

pages.title: Auto-Selling
pages.body:
OFF BY DEFAULT
Edit a draft on Auto-Sell: Hold Coins, Cover Operations or Fixed Share. Apply Draft and confirm to activate; Reload discards edits. Hold Coins is the default.

Cover Operations follows your coin order toward the next three nights' known power budget. Fixed Share caps the sale at 0%-100% of this night's new output, in 10% steps. Full execution is not guaranteed.

MINIMUM NET PRICE AND LEFTOVERS
The price floor uses whole-order net average after fees, slippage and cash rounding. Below-floor sales are skipped. Automatic sales run at the new day's quote after costs are paid and production is credited. Limited depth may fill part; unsold coins stay in the wallet.

Check next day's report for unsold reasons. Expected sale proceeds are not cash already available.

pages.title: Business Ledger
pages.body:
SEPARATE CASH, PRODUCTION AND HOLDINGS
The ledger retains 90 days. Cash flow records actual trades, operating/servicing costs, expansion and prepaid rent. Production records coins, pool fees and running costs. Reference holdings value and unrealized profit/loss change with prices; unsold coins are not realized cash income.

COUNT EQUIPMENT AND MATERIAL COSTS TOO
Purchased-coin cost includes fees and uses a weighted average. Mined coins have no purchase cost; power is listed separately. Sale quantities are attributed between mined and purchased coins in proportion to wallet holdings.

To calculate total returns, also include actual hardware purchase, repair and servicing-material spending. These costs are not fully tracked here, so ledger returns alone do not establish total profit or an exact payback date.
